dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: Maps x to the norm selected by Pi.normedRing on the finite function space Fin n → ℝ. Under the standard finite-Pi norm, this is the maximum coordinate magnitude max_i |x(i)|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its value N is assumed positive and occurs in the denominators and scaling bounds θ/(2N) < λ ≤ θ/N.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For λ ∈ ℝ, x : Fin n → ℝ, and i : Fin n, it returns the real product λx(i).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The two conclusions bound the absolute values |λx(i)|.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction of two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires both the uniform upper bound and the existential strict lower bound to hold simultaneously.

dependency_coverage.name: DivInvMonoid.toDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the division operation from a DivInvMonoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies real division for θ/(2N), θ/N, and θ/2.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification over a type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: States that at least one index i : Fin n satisfies θ/2 < |λx(i)|.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite type of natural-number indices strictly below n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes x an n-coordinate real vector and supplies the domains of the universal and existential index quantifiers.

dependency_coverage.name: HDiv.hDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: Applies the heterogeneous division operation provided by an HDiv instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses each quotient appearing in the hypotheses and conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Applies the heterogeneous multiplication operation provided by an HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses 2N in a denominator and the coordinate products λx(i).

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: Applies the non-strict order relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses 0 ≤ λ, λ ≤ θ/N, and |λx(i)| ≤ θ.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: Applies the strict order relation supplied by an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses n > 0, N > 0, θ/(2N) < λ, and θ/2 < |λx(i)|.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the dimension n and the natural literals used in elaborating 0, 1, and 2.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.instAtLeastTwoHAddOfNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a nonzero natural n, proves that n + 1 is at least two.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Participates only in constructing the real numeral 2; it introduces no mathematical hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.instNeZeroSucc
dependency_coverage.meaning: Proves that every natural-number successor n + 1 is nonzero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports the typeclass derivation used to construct the numeral 2.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Interprets a natural-number literal in a type equipped with the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Interprets the literals 0, 1, and 2 used throughout the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the scalar and coordinate type for x, λ, θ, norms, products, quotients, and inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Provides the additive-group structure on ℝ, including negation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the negation operation required by the definition of absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instDivInvMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Provides multiplication, inversion, division, and integer powers on ℝ; division is multiplication by an inverse.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes all displayed divisions ordinary real divisions.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: Provides the usual non-strict order ≤ on ℝ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Gives the intended meanings of all real-valued non-strict inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: Provides the usual strict order < on ℝ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Gives the intended meanings of all real-valued strict inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Provides ordinary multiplication on ℝ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Interprets 2N and λx(i) as real products.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instNatCast
dependency_coverage.meaning: Casts natural numbers into ℝ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Interprets the numeral 2 as the real number 2.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: Provides the real number zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Interprets the zero in 0 ≤ λ and 0 < N.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.meaning: Provides lattice operations, including maximum, for the ordered real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports the definition |a| = max(a, -a).

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: Converts a Zero instance into an interpretation of the numeral 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Allows real zero to be written as the literal 0 in the hypotheses.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.meaning: Defines absolute value by |a| = max(a, -a).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Measures the magnitude of each scaled coordinate λx(i) in both conclusions.

dependency_coverage.name: instHDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: Turns an ordinary homogeneous Div operation into an HDiv operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Routes each real quotient to ordinary real division.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Turns an ordinary homogeneous Mul operation into an HMul operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Routes 2N and λx(i) to ordinary real multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: instLTNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Provides the standard strict order on natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes the dimension hypothesis 0 < n mean that n is positive.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatAtLeastTwo
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a type with natural-number casts, interprets any literal n known to be at least two by casting n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Constructs the real literal 2 used in the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Interprets a natural-number literal n in Nat as n itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Elaborates the natural literals used in the dimension condition and in constructing the real numeral 2.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: Provides the finite enumeration of Fin n by the indices 0 through n - 1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Enables the finite-Pi normed-ring structure on Fin n → ℝ and the finite index quantifiers.

dependency_coverage.name: Norm.norm
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts and applies the real-valued norm operation from a Norm structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Evaluates the norm N = ‖x‖ used by LocalDef001.

dependency_coverage.name: NormedCommRing.toNormedRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: Forgets commutativity from a normed commutative ring, yielding a normed ring.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies each real coordinate with the NormedRing structure required to construct the Pi normed ring.

dependency_coverage.name: NormedRing.toNorm
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the Norm structure from a NormedRing structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the norm operation used on the function space Fin n → ℝ.

dependency_coverage.name: Pi.normedRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a normed-ring structure on a finitely indexed dependent function space from normed-ring structures on its coordinate types. Its norm is inherited from Pi.seminormedRing.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Selects the specific norm on Fin n → ℝ used by LocalDef001; under the standard finite-Pi construction this is the maximum of the coordinate norms.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.normedCommRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: Provides the normed commutative ring structure on ℝ, inheriting its norm from the real normed additive commutative group.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the coordinate norm and ring structure from which the finite-Pi norm of x is constructed; the standard coordinate norm is |a|.

binders: A real vector x represented as a function x : Fin n → ℝ.
hypotheses: The scale factor is nonnegative: 0 ≤ λ.
Writing N = ‖x‖ for LocalDef001 x, the vector norm is positive: 0 < N.
The strict lower scaling condition θ/(2N) < λ holds.
The non-strict upper scaling condition λ ≤ θ/N holds.
conclusions: For every index i : Fin n, |λx(i)| ≤ θ.
There exists an index i : Fin n such that θ/2 < |λx(i)|.
mathematical_definitions: Fin n is the index set {0, 1, ..., n - 1}.
N := LocalDef001 x is the norm of x supplied by the finite-Pi normed-ring instance. Under its standard semantics, N = max_{i : Fin n} |x(i)|.
|a| := max(a, -a), and all products, quotients, and order relations are those of the real numbers.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive integer dimension n, every real n-vector x with positive finite-Pi norm N, and all real numbers λ and θ, if λ is nonnegative and lies in the interval θ/(2N) < λ ≤ θ/N, then every scaled coordinate λx(i) has magnitude at most θ, while at least one scaled coordinate has magnitude strictly greater than θ/2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement is conditional: whenever any hypothesis fails, it makes no assertion for those parameter values.
The condition 0 < n excludes the empty index type and permits the existential conclusion to have a witness.
The condition 0 < ‖x‖ excludes the zero vector and ensures that the denominators ‖x‖ and 2‖x‖ are nonzero.

Although θ > 0 and λ > 0 are not explicit hypotheses, they follow whenever all hypotheses are simultaneously satisfied; consequently the assumptions are inconsistent, and the implication vacuous, when θ ≤ 0.
The lower conclusion applies to only one unspecified coordinate, not to every coordinate.
The inequalities are asymmetric and exact: the uniform upper bound is non-strict, whereas the existential lower bound is strict.
The statement is restricted to finite real vectors and the particular norm selected by Pi.normedRing; it does not quantify over arbitrary norms or scalar fields.
Lean division is total, but division-by-zero behavior is irrelevant here because the norm denominators and the constant denominator 2 are nonzero.
No approximation, rounding, floating-point operation, error model, or algorithmic computation is encoded in the proposition.
ambiguities: The supplied body of Pi.normedRing inherits its norm from Pi.seminormedRing, but the latter's definition is not supplied. Thus the packet fixes the Lean norm instance but does not itself expose a coordinate formula. The max-coordinate interpretation used in the translation is the standard finite-Pi interpretation, conditional on that inherited instance having its usual semantics.
